title: Nationalist Critique Of Colonial Economy
definition: The intellectual and economic analysis developed by 19th and early 20th-century Indian nationalist leaders (Early Nationalists/Moderates) demonstrating how British colonial policies systematically impoverished India by draining its wealth and subordinating its economic interests to British industrial capitalism.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for Modern Indian History (GS-1) and Economic History/Post-Independence Consolidation linkages (GS-3). Frequently tested in Prelims via key personalities, books, and drain theories, and in Mains regarding the economic impact of British rule.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Nationalist Critique Of Colonial Economy.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Foundational phases of British expansion in India
